headline: Divestiture trims revenue as cost cuts lift profit
summary_short: Gartner's Q2 FY2026 revenue was roughly flat at $1.676 billion (-0.6% y/y) following the February 2026 sale of its Digital Markets business, while diluted EPS rose 33.1% y/y to $4.14 on lower costs and a smaller share count.
summary_long: Revenue held flat at $1.676 billion as Insights (+2%) and Conferences (+15%) growth was offset by a 9% Consulting decline and the loss of Digital Markets revenue after its February 2026 sale. Cost of services fell 8% y/y on lower product/content delivery and headcount costs tied to that divestiture, lifting operating income 15.9% to $379.3 million. Net income rose 14.4% to $275.5 million; diluted EPS climbed 33.1% to $4.14, helped by a smaller diluted share count after $547.1 million of buybacks this quarter. Cash fell to $1.489 billion and long-term debt held near $3.0 billion following the 2031/2035 notes issued in November 2025. No forward guidance is disclosed in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Insights (+2%) and Conferences (+15%) growth was offset by a 9% Consulting decline (Japan/EMEA commercial weakness) and the February 2026 Digital Markets divestiture.
Decrease driven by lower product and content delivery expense and lower personnel expense, both tied to the Digital Markets sale and reduced headcount.
Increase was primarily due to the reduction in operating expenses (cost of services and SG&A), per the release's own explanation.
Higher net income reflects lower operating expenses, partially offset by a revenue decline and higher net interest expense from the 2031/2035 notes.
Diluted EPS growth outpaced net income growth because of a smaller diluted weighted-average share count from continued buybacks.
Board authorized an incremental $500 million share-repurchase program in July 2026, on top of $8.1 billion previously authorized with ~$640 million remaining.
